free_tier.stated: Epho's own page states a 'starting credit: $10 on signup — roughly 60 hours of the default instance'. Sandbox resources are metered per second from boot to teardown: CPU $0.0000164 per vCPU-second, memory $0.0000053 per GiB-second, disk $0.000000036 per GiB-second. The default instance is 2 vCPU, 2 GiB and 10 GiB at about $0.0000438 per second, or about $0.0026 for a one-minute run. No monthly plan fee is stated.
free_tier.notes: The 10 dollars is a starting credit, not a recurring monthly allowance. Model tokens are never billed by Epho; they ride on the caller's provider_api_key at the provider's price. A turn is refused with 402 once the Epho credit balance reaches zero.

per_object_cap.stated: Not an object store: the default sandbox is 2 vCPU, 2 GiB RAM and 10 GiB disk. A request accepts up to 32 repos and up to 20 input files, and produced files come back as artifacts with a presigned URL good for about ten minutes.
per_object_cap.notes: The instance object in the API lets the caller size the box, so CPU, memory and disk are configurable.

retention.stated: Nothing idles, nothing is stored, nothing keeps billing: the sandbox stops when a turn ends. A chat keeps its filesystem and agent session across turns; if the box is gone, a replacement boots and the agent session snapshot is restored. Artifact download URLs expire about ten minutes after the event.
retention.notes: No retention period in days is published; the sandbox is torn down at the end of each turn.

egress.terms: No egress price or allowance is stated: the meter prices sandbox CPU, memory and disk per second, and produced files are returned through presigned download URLs against an otherwise-private bucket that expire about ten minutes after the event. Outbound network access from the sandbox is not priced separately on the page.

interface_detail: One HTTP endpoint, POST /api/v1/chat with a JSON body, returns text/event-stream; POST /api/v1/chat/async queues the turn; GET /chat/{id}/events/subscribe replays and live-tails persisted events. API base https://app.epho.io/api.
tooling: curl or any HTTP client, no SDK required; the quickstart shows curl -N with an Epho API key and a provider API key.
chaining: A team API key scopes the work, a provider_api_key pays the model tokens at the provider's own price, and the chat_id resumes the same sandbox and agent session on the next turn.

limits_note: Per chat only one turn may be active; another turn started before the first settles returns 409 Conflict. A request accepts up to 32 repos and up to 20 input files.
binding_note: The 10-dollar credit is the first limit an individual user meets: the default instance burns about 0.0026 dollars per minute, so roughly 60 hours of compute, and a turn is refused with 402 when the balance reaches zero.

identity_cost.detail: The registration form asks for Name, Email address, Password and Confirm password, and offers Google or GitHub sign-in. Registration was read in an archived capture because the live /register URL redirects to a login wall. The 10-dollar starting credit appears in the app's login page props as 'verifiedBonusDollars': 10; whether verification gates the bonus is unverified: behind a sign-up.

reliability_note: The sandbox is torn down at the end of each turn; an interrupted pipe does not kill a run because events are persisted and the stream can be re-subscribed. An artifact URL expires about ten minutes after it is emitted.
confidence_note: Rates, credit, default instance, token billing, meter semantics, artifact lifetime and free-model option are quoted from Epho's own page read 2026-11-24; the concurrency cap, 409 rule and API shape come from the first-party docs. The signup form is quoted from an archived capture because all live routes to /register were walled. Account-only terms such as verification for the bonus are unverified: behind a sign-up.

notes: Epho is a hosted agent API: the user sends a prompt and Epho boots and tears down the sandbox, so nothing is installed or operated by the user. The 10-dollar credit is a start bonus, not a recurring free tier; the metered resource is sandbox wall-clock, and model tokens bill on a key the caller supplies. The live /register page redirects to a login wall, so the signup form was read from an archived capture.
